exam: 2023年6月 第2套 · 仔细阅读 P1
title: Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest…

sents.en: Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit.
sents.cn: 长期以来，超市一直处境艰难：它是现存利润率最薄的行业之一，也是最不受人期待的工作或光顾场所之一。

sents.en: For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change.
sents.cn: 十多年来，它们受到电商巨头的冲击，被指责让美国人变胖，并被指控加剧了气候变化。

sents.en: Supermarkets can technically be defined as giants housing 15,000 to 60,000 different products.
sents.cn: 从技术上讲，超市可被定义为陈列15,000到60,000种不同商品的巨型场所。

sents.en: The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America.
sents.cn: 自助式杂货店这一革命性理念——人们可以在过道里自行"狩猎"、采集食物，而不必让店员从柜台后取货——最早出现在美国。

sents.en: There is some debate about which was the very first, but over the years a consensus has built around King Kullen Supermarket, founded in New York in 1930.
sents.cn: 关于哪家才是第一家，存在一些争议，但多年来，人们逐渐达成了共识：1930年成立于纽约的KingKullen超市是首家。

sents.en: For some 300 years, Americans had fed themselves from small stores and public markets.
sents.cn: 约300年里，美国人一直靠小商店和公共市场获取食物。

sents.en: Shopping for food involved mud, noisy chickens, clouds of flies, nasty smells, bargaining, and getting short-changed.
sents.cn: 买食物意味着泥泞、聒噪的鸡群、成团的苍蝇、难闻的气味、讨价还价，以及被少找零钱。

sents.en: The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food.
sents.cn: 超市模仿了福特式工厂对效率和标准化的强调，并把它重新想象成一个购买食物的场所。

sents.en: Supermarkets may not feel cutting-edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time.
sents.cn: 超市如今或许已不让人觉得前沿，但在当时它是一场分销革命。

sents.en: They were such strange marvels that, on her first official state visit to the United States in 1957, Queen Elizabeth II insisted on an impromptu tour of a suburban-Maryland Giant Food.
sents.cn: 它们是如此奇特的奇迹，以至于1957年伊丽莎白二世女王首次对美国进行正式国事访问时，坚持要即兴参观马里兰州郊区的一家GiantFood超市。

sents.en: The typical supermarket layout has barely changed over the past 90 years.
sents.cn: 典型的超市布局在过去90年里几乎没有改变。

sents.en: Most stores open with flowers, fruit and vegetables at the front as a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite.
sents.cn: 大多数商店把鲜花、水果和蔬菜摆在前方开场，作为一缕清新来唤起我们的食欲。

sents.en: Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you'll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way.
sents.cn: 与此同时，它们把牛奶、鸡蛋和其他日常必需品放在最里头，好让你尽可能穿过更多店面，一路受到诱惑。

sents.en: In the early days, as the supermarket multiplied, so did our suspicion of it.
sents.cn: 在早期，随着超市成倍增加，我们对它的怀疑也随之增长。

sents.en: We have long feared that this "revolution in distribution" uses corporate black magic on our appetite.
sents.cn: 我们一直担心，这场"分销革命"在对我们的食欲使用企业的黑魔法。

sents.en: The book The Hidden Persuaders, published in 1957, warned that supermarkets were putting women in a "hypnoidal trance," causing them to wander aisles bumping into boxes and "picking things off shelves at random."
sents.cn: 1957年出版的《隐性说服者》一书警告说，超市正把女性置于一种"催眠恍惚状态"，让她们在过道里游荡、撞上纸箱，并"随手从货架上乱拿东西"。
